targetAudience.primary: Open-source maintainers and engineers responsible for resource-manager lifecycle reliability
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands connection managers, cleanup, retries and object identity.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Duplicate resource entries can trigger repeated connect and cleanup side effects, while ad hoc deduplication across lifecycle methods produces inconsistent ownership semantics.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Agents Python change canonicalizes repeated MCP server entries before manager ownership and reuses the same uniqueness helper across connect, retry and cleanup paths.

externalHook.description: A manager should decide which resources it owns before the first connect, retry or cleanup side effect occurs.

coreProposition: Resource managers should establish one canonical owned population before lifecycle side effects and reuse one documented identity relation across connect, retry and cleanup; deduplication and serialized mutation improve in-process accounting but do not establish endpoint uniqueness or distributed exactly-once execution.

originalValue.description: Moves deduplication from per-operation repair into the ownership boundary, separates population identity from temporal serialization, and defines the evidence needed before making stronger exactly-once claims.

readerTakeaway: Canonicalize once before ownership, document whether uniqueness means object identity, equality or a logical key, and test every lifecycle phase without promoting local call counts into distributed guarantees.

supported: MCPServerManager canonicalizes incoming entries before lifecycle ownership.
The helper preserves first-occurrence order and uses set/equality membership.
The repeated-object regression observes one connect and one cleanup.
Lifecycle mutation is serialized by a process-local lock.
unsupported: Correctness for every custom equality implementation
uncertain: Whether uniqueness should use identity, equality or a logical resource key
How intentionally separate sessions to one endpoint should be represented

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general resource-lifecycle ownership pattern without first-party project dependence.

decisionReason: The merged implementation and regression supply a concrete ownership defect, and the Research Object adds a transferable identity and guarantee model.
